title: Coherent precomposition of module operation trees
statement:
Use the quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], the ordered-fibre category $L=N(\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes})$, its pure-algebra part $A$, coherent left tensorings and module sections of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], and the operation-tree and parameterized transformation data of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction]. Let $\mathcal V$ be a monoidal infinity-category, $\mathcal M$ coherently left-tensored over it by $q:E^\otimes\to L$, let $B,C:A\to E^\otimes|_A$ be associative algebra sections, let $h:B\to C$ be a coherent algebra transformation, and let $L_C:L\to E^\otimes$ be a module section restricting to $C$. Write $x=L_C(m)$ and $b^{L_C}_r:C^{\otimes r}\otimes x\to x$ for its ordered module operations, for every $r\geq0$. On the color objects $B$ and $x$, the operations
$$b^h_r=b^{L_C}_r\circ(h^{\otimes r}\otimes1_x)$$
admit a full homotopy coherent substitution system: comparison simplices for every finite operation-labeled rooted tree and every chain of contractions, compatible with faces, degeneracies, grafting, permutations and insertion of identities. Its pure-algebra part is the specified section $B$. The empty algebra subtree uses the unit compatibility of $h$, and $b^h_0$ is the identity constraint on $x$.

These systems include compatible transformation data to $L_C$, whose pure-algebra component is $h$ and whose module-color component is $1_x$. On a chain of contractions of a module-output tree, this system is obtained by evaluating the coherent transformation $h$ on each pure-algebra subtree, evaluating the substitution data of $L_C$ along the unique module branch, and composing using the specified tensor/action coherences with a common diagonal restriction of parameters. This assignment supplies the full tree comparisons, not just the binary action equations. It is compatible with restriction in every simplicial parameter: for a family $h$ and $L_C$ over any simplicial set $K$, it gives such operation and transformation data over $K$. The associated total inert arrows are $q$-cocartesian. No colimit, limit or presentability hypothesis is imposed.
